title: Vivaticket announces partnership with Baskonia-Alavés Group
summary:
Vivaticket, a leading ticketing and access control solution provider, has been named the official ticketing platform for the sports management organisation, Baskonia-Alavés Group.

As the Group continues its digital transformation, Vivaticket will handle ticket and season ticket sales across its entities, offering fans and users a quicker, safer, and more intuitive purchasing journey.

Streamlined processes

Starting this season, the new platform will streamline ticket and season ticket management for Baskonia, Deportivo Alavés, and Deportivo Alavés Gloriosas matches, with tools that will support both internal operations and the user purchasing process.

See also: Connecting culture and technology: Vivaticket’s next chapter in Spain

Haritz Kerejeta, CEO of the Baskonia-Alavés Group, says: "We continue to work to provide our fans with the best possible service.

"The addition of Vivaticket represents an important step forward in our digital transformation process and will allow us to have a more modern, flexible platform that is better equipped to meet the current and future needs of our competitions and events."

The new plaform will offer fans and users a simplified process and enhanced digital experienceImage courtesy of Vivaticket

"We are delighted to begin this new chapter alongside the Baskonia-Alavés Group," says Silvano Taiani, CEO of Vivaticket.

"We will work closely together to continue driving innovation in sports ticketing and make it easier for fans to enjoy, at all times, what they are passionate about."

The new system will progressively introduce new features designed to improve the relationship with fans, simplify purchasing processes and strengthen the digital experience around events organised by the Baskonia-Alavés Group.

Vivaticket has a proven track record in live music, theatre, museums, fairs, theme parks, and sports. With this partnership, the company builds on its established presence at some of Europe’s leading clubs, sports venues and events.

Earlier this year, Vivaticket was named as the official and exclusive technology partner for ticketing for Real Betis Balompié, in an agreement that extends through seven seasons.

title: From SEA Expo to Connex: a new approach to Saudi Arabia’s attractions market
summary:
SEA Expo has brought together the manufacturers, suppliers, developers and operators shaping Saudi Arabia’s leisure and entertainment industry for almost a decade. As the industry continues to grow, so does the value of bringing its senior leaders together for focused conversations, shared insight and time to build relationships.

SEA Expo Connex 2026 has been created to meet that need.

Building on SEA Expo’s established industry connections, the new format brings operators, developers, investors and suppliers together for two days of networking, project discussions and behind-the-scenes experiences.


Taking place on 21–22 October at Six Flags Qiddiya City and Aquarabia Qiddiya City, the event puts delegates inside the destinations shaping Saudi Arabia’s entertainment ambitions.

From discussions around the table to conversations during guided tours, the programme gives attendees more time together to exchange ideas, explore partnerships and understand the opportunities ahead.

Blooloop speaks with Sarkis Kahwajian, associate VP at dmg events, about the thinking behind SEA Expo Connex, the changing needs of Saudi Arabia’s attractions sector, and the decision to make Qiddiya the event's setting.

He discusses the opportunities across the regional events market, the progress of projects from planning to delivery, and how a focused, on-site format can bring the attractions industry closer together.

​Why SEA Expo Connex?


Saudi Arabia’s growing attractions industry has created a need for more time together: time to discuss projects in detail, share operational experience, and build relationships among the people developing, supplying, and running its entertainment destinations.

SEA Expo Connex meets that need by adding a new format to the established SEA Expo platform.


This approach reflects how dmg events has developed its portfolio alongside the industry. The launches of Saudi Light and Sound (SLS) Expo and Merath Expo, the Middle East Heritage and Museums Expo, have given specialist communities dedicated platforms while maintaining connections across the wider industry.

Kahwajian points to technology as one of those shared interests:

“Technology is the connection that all of them have,” he says, highlighting the use of virtual reality, large displays, holograms, theming and lighting across museums, live entertainment and theme parks.

With more attractions moving from development to operations, there is plenty for this community to discuss.

SEA Expo Connex provides a dedicated setting for those conversations, building on the relationships formed through SEA Expo and bringing senior figures together around shared interests and upcoming opportunities.

“The real value of an event is not just what happens on the exhibition floor,” Kahwajian says. “It's the conversations, the relationships, and the connections that happen around it.”

The programme brings together executives, project directors, operators and government leaders for industry discussions, networking and behind-the-scenes experiences at Six Flags Qiddiya City and Aquarabia Qiddiya City.


The venues give delegates a first-hand perspective on destination development and operations, with time to exchange ideas as they explore.

“We built this community over the last 10 years, and we wanted to keep that momentum going by creating another opportunity for the industry to come together.

“That meant looking at what would add value for them now. With SEA Expo Connex, we saw an opportunity to bring senior industry figures together inside the destinations everyone is talking about, giving them time to share ideas, discuss projects and build relationships as they explore.

“We wanted to create a premium experience that builds on those existing connections and opens the door to new ones.”

As an addition to the SEA Expo portfolio, SEA Expo Connex gives the industry another way to meet and work together. Its value lies in bringing the right people into the same setting, with the time and access to turn shared interests into lasting business relationships.

​What can attendees expect from SEA Expo Connex?


The agenda brings together senior figures from across the attractions, entertainment and leisure sectors for two days of discussion focused on the practical challenges and opportunities shaping Saudi Arabia’s rapidly developing entertainment industry.

The programme combines industry insight with the opportunity to experience major projects from behind the scenes.

The speaker line-up includes leaders from operators, developers, suppliers and entertainment organisations, including Dr Neil Dwyer, VP operations at Six Flags Qiddiya City; Bianca Sammut, executive director at Saudi Entertainment Ventures (SEVEN); Faisal Hakami, general manager, MENA operations at Al Othaim Entertainment; and Mohamed Attia, founder and CEO of Ground Control Entertainment.

Attendees will also hear from Peter Boyack, executive VP of business development at WhiteWater; Angela Selkirk, executive director of events and experience at MDLBEAST; and Dr Eihab Abourokbah, CEO of Saudi Entertainment and Event Management Academy.


View this post on Instagram

A post shared by SEA Expo (@saudientertainmentexpo)

Across the programme, discussions will explore how successful entertainment destinations are developed and operated, from the partnerships, investment and talent required to build the wider entertainment ecosystem to the operational considerations involved in creating memorable guest experiences.

Workforce development and the skills needed to support Saudi Arabia’s next phase of entertainment growth are also key themes.

A particular focus on Qiddiya City runs through the agenda.

Day One examines the ambition and leadership decisions behind Six Flags Qiddiya City, while Day Two turns to the development of Aquarabia, including the factors that contribute to successful large-scale destinations, from planning through to operations and guest loyalty.

Guided educational tours complement the conference sessions. On the first day, delegates will go behind the scenes at Six Flags Qiddiya City, including experiencing Falcon’s Flight, before exploring the park.

On Day Two, delegates will visit Aquarabia Qiddiya City for a guided tour examining the design, operational, and guest-experience considerations behind the waterpark.

​Finding the right host in Six Flags Qiddiya City


To host SEA Expo Connex, dmg events partnered with Six Flags Qiddiya City, one of the most ambitious entertainment, sports, and cultural destinations in recent history, and home to attractions such as Falcon's Flight, the world's tallest, longest, and fastest roller coaster.

For Kahwajian, partnering with Six Flags Qiddiya City was an essential decision that aligns with what global industry leaders now expect from Saudi market engagements.

"The biggest difference with SEA Expo Connex is that it is designed around the people and the experience rather than the exhibition space.

"We want people to go away having had the conversations that they would normally have in a traditional conference, but in an environment where some of the most significant developments are actually happening. That's why we chose Qiddiya City."


Holding SEA Expo Connex at Qiddiya City also gives delegates the opportunity to see projects progressing beyond the renderings and discuss their development in context.

"You can sit in a conference room anywhere, but when you actually have an event at a venue in Qiddiya City, attendees are right there where the vision is coming to life. Qiddiya really represents where the Saudi attraction industry is headed.

"It is difficult to find a better example of the scale and ambition of what is being developed in the Kingdom.

“Six Flags Qiddiya City is particularly relevant to our industry because it brings together major international brands, cutting-edge technologies, complex ride engineering, operations, and an entirely new destination concept."

Kahwajian sees the on-site format as an important part of that proposition:

“That is one of the main reasons we created SEA Expo Connex. After years of announcements, industry leaders want to see the destinations for themselves and understand, from the teams running them, how they will operate in practice.”

​From master planning to operations


One of the biggest changes in Saudi Arabia's attractions market is the shift from master planning to operational delivery. Five to seven years ago, much of the industry conversation centred on major announcements, conceptual renders and long-term plans.

As major projects move toward completion and opening, the focus is shifting to operational readiness, guest experience, asset maintenance, and workforce development.

"A few years ago, a lot of discussion was about what was going to be built.

"Now, there is much more focus on how these destinations are going to operate: how you attract visitors, how you manage the guest experience, how you recruit and train local talent, how you maintain complex assets, and how you create destinations that people want to return to again and again."


That shift is also changing what developers and operators expect from suppliers. A good product is no longer enough. Companies also need to understand the Saudi market, its operational requirements and the need for long-term local support and maintenance.

“We are also seeing a much more diverse ecosystem developing around the major projects, which creates opportunities well beyond traditional attraction suppliers."

That transition also changes the conversations suppliers and operators need to have. SEA Expo Connex is intended to provide a smaller setting for those conversations, bringing senior operational, engineering and park leaders together to discuss issues such as ride safety, queue management, guest comfort and F&B.

​Listening to the market


dmg events organises around 85 exhibitions worldwide, including around 40 in Saudi Arabia, giving it a broad view of the markets in which it operates.

Kahwajian says the organisation's role is to listen to the industry and develop platforms around the needs it identifies:

"I don't claim to be an expert in the attractions industry. We organise exhibitions, and our job is to become part of and speak the language of whatever industry we are catering to.

"But we in no way become the operators or designers ourselves. It’s the people on the ground going through the intricacies of what that industry entails; they are the real experts."


That approach has shaped the development of SEA Expo Connex. Rather than setting the agenda independently, dmg events says it consulted Saudi project leaders, international OEMs and local operational teams about the issues they wanted to discuss.

"All we do is provide a platform and try to keep our finger on the pulse of what's happening as much as we can. These smaller, focused conferences are the best way to do that.

"It’s about having the right conversations with the right people and understanding what they actually want to discuss, not what our conference producers think is trendy.

“We have to listen to the industry. We create the platform; they do all the hard work."

​​What international suppliers need to know


For international suppliers, design firms and technology providers, SEA Expo Connex offers an opportunity to understand the Saudi market first-hand and connect with the people shaping its growth.

Kahwajian highlights the value of building lasting relationships and investing time in a long-term presence in the Kingdom:

"The biggest opportunity SEA Expo Connex creates for international companies is understanding the market in depth. Saudi Arabia is attracting enormous global interest, but entering the market successfully requires much more than simply identifying a project online and sending in a sales team.

“Companies need to understand who the actual decision-makers are, how the ecosystem functions, what the local regulatory requirements are, and where the real gaps lie."


View this post on Instagram

A post shared by SEA Expo (@saudientertainmentexpo)

He adds that suppliers entering the market need to consider local cultural expectations, climate conditions and operational requirements rather than assuming that products developed elsewhere can be transferred directly.

"Sometimes the most valuable thing an international supplier can do when entering a new market is to sit back and listen.

"Understand what the market actually needs rather than trying to sell whatever product you happen to have in your portfolio. Saudi Arabia is more intricate than most other markets.

"You really have to be on the ground, be part of the ongoing conversation, and meet people face to face to understand what the industry is looking for."

SEA Expo Connex is intended to create opportunities for international delegates to meet Saudi procurement managers, master planners and operational leaders in a smaller setting.

Kahwajian says SEA Expo Connex is here to complement SEA Expo.

"SEA Expo is our major, macro-level industry platform and trade marketplace. But the addition of SEA Expo Connex gives us the agility to experiment with different, highly focused formats, smaller, more experienced, and more intimate.

“SEA Expo Connex is here to complement the trade show ecosystem and ensure that the conversation never stops."

SEA Expo Connex 2026 will take place at Six Flags Qiddiya City from 21 - 22 October, providing a more focused counterpart to SEA Expo as Saudi Arabia's attractions market moves further into delivery and operations.

title: Thorpe Park's first-ever out-of-attraction Fright Nights experience launches for one day only
summary:
Thorpe Park has launched its first-ever out-of-attraction Fright Nights experience as the Halloween event celebrates its 25th anniversary.

Running for one night only on Saturday 3 October 2026, the Surrey theme park will offer an immersive blackout bus experience that extends the story of its new pitch-black scare maze, Tenement.

The Nova Lux Express will transport a select number of passengers on an almost pitch-black journey from Staines Railway Station to Nova Lux Senior Living, the abandoned building at the heart of Tenement.

Fright Nights at Thorpe Park features scare mazes, zones, live shows and after-dark coaster rides Merlin Entertainments

As the bus plunges into near darkness, passengers will learn more about the abandoned care home at the centre of Tenement.

Riders will take on the role of electricians sent to fix its persistent power problems, following a previous crew that lost contact with the outside world days earlier.

Thorpe Park vice president Ruth Storey said: "Fright Nights is the home of fear but this year we're taking that further than ever - literally, beyond the park’s gates.

"For the first time in Fright Nights history, the story doesn't start when you walk through the entrance, it starts the moment you step on board the Nova Lux Express."

She added: "The Nova Lux Express will transport guests straight into the world of Tenement before they've even arrived, so by the time they reach the park, they're already inside the story.

Fright Nights at Thorpe Park features scare mazes, zones, live shows and after-dark coaster rides Merlin Entertainments

"Tenement itself is our darkest scare maze yet, and after 25 years of Fright Nights, we wanted this anniversary to be the one that truly gets under people's skin."

Up to 14 travellers can board Nova Lux Express at Staines Railway Station, with departures running hourly from 14:00 to 17:00 on a first-come, first-served basis. Passengers must have tickets for Fright Nights and Tenement to travel.

Announced earlier this month, Tenement is a pitch-black scare maze set in an abandoned building where the tenants have vanished. Guests navigate the darkness using a shared handheld light that gradually fails.

title: Breeze Creative reveals Selfie Wall AI shared interactive attraction
summary:
Breeze Creative, a leading interactive product company creating innovative installations that combine technology, play, and education, has shared details of its latest product, Selfie Wall AI, which turns visitor photos into a playful, shared interactive attraction for family entertainment centres (FECs), resorts, attractions, and events.

In this AI-powered photo experience, visitors take a selfie at a touchscreen kiosk and watch their image transform into a character or scene on a large, evolving communal wall. Visitors can also receive their selfie by email as a souvenir.

For operators, this presents an opportunity to increase engagement in traditionally passive spaces, such as lobbies or waiting areas.

AI-generated selfies and photo booths are increasingly prevalent across the attractions and entertainment sector.

Selfie Wall takes this idea and makes it social. Instead of simply asking visitors to take an individual photo, it invites them to become part of something bigger.

The community wall keeps evolving as more guests participate. As visitors find their image among the growing collection of characters and transformations, the shared discovery creates natural social interaction around the technology.

"We wanted to move beyond the traditional photo booth experience," says Breeze Creative. "The idea is to create something people experience together, where every new participant adds something to the attraction."

Developed for different venues and different stories

Selfie Wall offers a shared, multi-generational experience where children can participate alongside teens, parents, and grandparents, making it suitable for a broad range of applications.

To make the concept even more versatile, the product uses a wide range of technologies, from an existing TV or projector to a larger video wall, depending on the venue's space, budget, and desired visual impact.

Its content library also lets venues tailor the experience to their audience and brand. Current themes include Comic Book, Art Gallery, and Fantasy World.

The growing Selfie Wall content library includes Comic Book, Art Gallery, and Fantasy WorldImage courtesy of Breeze Creative

Breeze Creative plans to continue expanding the library, with upcoming concepts including underwater environments, animals, holiday experiences and other themed worlds.

The aim is for the technology to feel less like a generic photo booth and more like a themed attraction created specifically for the environment.

Example applications include FECs seeking an interactive attraction with broad age appeal, hotels and resorts looking to entertain guests in lobbies, restaurants and waiting areas, and theme parks and attractions exploring personalised guest experiences.

For zoos and aquariums, Selfie Wall can be implemented with animal and underwater themes, while at museums and cultural attractions it can feature art, history, or storytelling themes. Visitor centres and hospitality venues can use the product to create a stronger welcome experience.

Additionally, restaurants can entertain families while they wait, shopping and retail destinations can add interactive experiences, and special events and brand activations can deliver a memorable AI-powered photo experience.

Engagement also extends beyond the physical visit, with the option for visitors to email the AI-generated photo to themselves as a digital souvenir to share on social media.

Turning guest engagement into measurable data

For attractions and entertainment venues, understanding what happens after a guest interacts with experiential technology is key. To address this, the Selfie Wall includes an operator dashboard that provides engagement data.

Operators can track participation and see how many guests choose to receive their AI-generated image by email compared to those who skip the feature. That data can help venues evaluate the installation's performance and understand how the visitors engage with the experience.

Selfie Wall offers a shared guest experience that growswith every participantImage courtesy of Breeze Creative

With appropriate consent and privacy practices, the email functionality can also help operators build a first-party marketing audience from guests who actively choose to share their contact information.

This blend of physical interaction, digital content, and measurable engagement makes Selfie Wall particularly relevant for operators looking beyond entertainment alone.

Earlier this month, Breeze Creative shared details of its project with ICR Discovery Center in Dallas to develop engaging, hands-on activities that inspire children and families to explore science through play, creativity, and discovery.
